title: R' Yudan Beribi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the end of Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 36, he reports R' Berechyah: ‘If you see the merit of the ancestors [שמחה],’ etc. Hyman says a scribal error occurred there: the teaching derives from Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1, where the name is correctly given as R' Yudan bar Chanin, reporting R' Berechyah.

notes.text: The supplied quote has שמחה, which does not mean ceased. Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin10:1 has שמטה, “has faltered,” and names Yudan bar Chanan; the notice has bar Chanin. The damaged quote and name difference remain open.

The earlier Sanhedrin10:1 consultation read שמטה, has faltered, and Yudan bar Chanan; it is inherited rather than a new whole primary read. Supplied שמחה does not mean ceased, while older machine שמתה is another form. The VayikraRabbah36 ending and Beribi heading remain unverified; Beribi is not expanded into invented parentage. Hyman’s claim of scribal error and his correctly-given bar Chanin reading retain their force as his argument. Exact uninspected personal title markers remain R'; neither name nor damaged quotation is silently repaired.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 619) reads שמתה, “has died out,” where the supplied Hebrew has שמחה. The consulted Hebrew of Vayikra Rabbah 36:6 and Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1 reads שמטה, “has faltered.” The former gives Rabbi Yudan Beribi in the name of Rabbi Berechyah, while the latter gives Rabbi Yudan bar Chanan in the same teacher’s name. Hyman prints bar Chanin and argues that the Jerusalem Talmud gives the correct name.
